proof_summary: Legendre’s formula expresses each prime-adic valuation as a sum of nonnegative floor-function defects; when a prime power dividing one of the odd linear factors exceeds \(3(2r+1)\), the resulting congruence and parity conditions force the corresponding defect to be at least one. Such a large prime power can divide at most one factor, while all smaller prime-power contributions are absorbed by choosing \(K=((3(2r+1))!)^r\), so summing valuations yields the required divisibility.
